skill_traces.query:
John: Hey Tim, been a while! How ya been?
Tim: Hey John! Great to hear from you. Been busy with things, how about you?
John: Yeah, something cool happened! I attended a local restaurant with some new teammates last week. It was great getting to know them better.
Tim: Good support is essential. How do you feel about them?
John: They're great friends. We connected over our shared love for basketball and had a ton of fun.
Tim: Sounds awesome. Having friends who share your hobbies can be really fun. Any exciting plans with them?
John: We're planning to take a team trip next month to explore a new city and have some fun. Can't wait!
Tim: That sounds great! Exploring new cities is always so much fun. Where are you headed?
John: We're still deciding on the destination. Do you have any suggestions?
Tim: Edinburgh, Scotland would be great for a magical vibe. It's the birthplace of Harry Potter and has awesome history and architecture. Plus, it's a beautiful city. What do you think?
John: That sounds like a great idea! I haven't been to Edinburgh yet, but it definitely sounds like a place worth considering for our trip. Thanks for the suggestion!
Tim: Glad you liked it. Let me know if you need any more suggestions.
John: Thanks! I'll definitely reach out if I need more suggestions. Appreciate the help! Here's a pic I snapped during one of our practices. The sunset looked amazing on the court. Moments like these make me so grateful for my basketball career.
Tim: Wow, that looks amazing! What do you love most about your basketball career?
John: Thanks! I love playing pro ball - it's a constant challenge and keeps me growing. There's nothing like seeing myself get better and beating goals. Plus, playing with my teammates and having the fans cheer is awesome. Basketball gives me a great sense of satisfaction and purpose.
Tim: It's great that you have a passion that helps you grow and reach your goals. Achieving and feeling fulfilled must be amazing. Do you have any specific targets or goals you're working towards?
John: Definitely! I'm focusing on better shooting and making more of an impact on the court. I want to be known as a consistent performer and help my team. Off the court, I'm also looking into more endorsements and building my brand. It's important for me to think about life after basketball.
Tim: Awesome! It's great that you have goals both on and off the court. It's wise to think about the future and building your brand. What are your thoughts on life after basketball?
John: I've thought about it a lot. I want to use my platform to make a positive difference and inspire others - maybe even start a foundation and do charity work. It's important to me to make the most of the chances I get and leave a meaningful legacy.
Tim: Wow, that's amazing. Good on you for wanting to make a difference and motivate others. I'm sure you'll succeed! Is there anything I can do to support you?
John: Thanks! I'm trying to figure out how to pick the right ones - any advice on that?
Tim: When picking endorsements, make sure they align with your values and brand. Look for a company that shares your desire to make a change and help others. It's important that the endorsement feels authentic to your followers.
John: Sounds like good advice! I was wondering if you have any book recommendations for my trip?
Tim: Yeah! I think you'd love this fantasy novel by Patrick Rothfuss. It's a book that'll take you to a different world. Great for you when you're traveling. Have fun!
John: Thanks! I'll definitely check it out - looks like a great book to read while traveling. Can't wait to dive into it! Here's a photo of my bookshelf. You can see some of the books I've read and enjoyed.
Tim: Great bookshelf! I saw that you had "The Alchemist" on there, one of my favorites. Did you enjoy it?
John: Yep, I read that book and loved it! It made me think about life and how important it is to follow one's dreams. Highly recommend it!
Tim: Glad you liked it! "The Alchemist" is worth it.
John: Thanks! Take care!
Tim: Have fun! Take care and talk to you soon.

selected.name: Extract Explicit Advice and Suggestions
selected.description: When a message contains explicit advice, suggestions, or recommendations from one participant to another, extract them as memory candidates.
content: During extraction, treat explicit advice, suggestions, and recommendations as memory-worthy. Capture the advisor, the recipient, the advised action, and the source message.
Preserve all distinct pieces of advice and their qualifiers; do not collapse or omit details. Tentative phrasing still counts.
Represent as an event or relationship memory; create at most one candidate per distinct piece of advice.
Stop after capturing the stated advice; do not infer outcomes or expand into related topics.
selected.rerank_reason: The session contains explicit advice from Tim to John about selecting endorsements that align with his values and brand, which qualifies for extraction as per the skill's procedure.

selected.name: Extract Explicit Goals and Intended Impact
selected.description: Use when a message states a hope, goal, dream, or intended impact for an activity or interest.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly states a user's goal, hope, aspiration, or intended impact for an activity (e.g., share stories, make a difference, reach others), capture it as a separate facet in the memory content; do not replace it with only current emotional benefits like escape, expression, or healing.
When enriching an existing memory, preserve previously stored facets and ADD the newly stated goal or impact rather than overwriting the memory with a narrower paraphrase.
Stop after capturing the explicit goal and its immediate context; do not enumerate every possible future hope or infer unstated ambitions.
selected.rerank_reason: John explicitly states his goals related to improving his basketball skills and making an impact on the court, as well as his aspirations off the court, which fits the skill's focus on extracting explicit goals and intended impact.

nearby_not_selected.name: Location Qualifiers for Named Destination Plans
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting or updating a plan memory that mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, include its commonly known location(s) so future location questions can be answered.
content: During extraction, if a plan memory mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, add a concise qualifier naming its well-known location(s), e.g., US states or countries.
Use only common knowledge about that entity; do not research or speculate beyond obvious, widely known locations.
If one location is commonly known, record it; if several prominent locations exist, record all commonly known ones, then stop.
Apply the same qualifier when updating an existing plan memory that references the venue.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract implied vacation location memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user mentions a past vacation or trip with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), extract an event memory for that time and place, resolving relative time from the message timestamp.
content: During extraction, if a message mentions a trip or vacation with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), create an event memory for that trip. Resolve the relative time from the message timestamp; use the country as the location if only a city is named.
Do not skip such statements just because the trip is mentioned as background (e.g., describing a photo). If the location and time are clear, extract the event.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Offers, Encouragement, and Advice
nearby_not_selected.description: Use during extraction when a message contains one person offering help, giving advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
content: During extraction, treat a single message as sufficient evidence when a speaker offers help, gives advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
Create one event memory capturing the speaker, the recipient, and the gist of what was said, including any explicit guidance or offer topic.
Stop after the gist is captured; do not infer the recipient's internal feelings or expand into multiple memory kinds unless the message contains other distinct facts.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture likely deceased from euphemistic absence language
nearby_not_selected.description: During extraction, when a speaker describes someone with euphemistic absence language (e.g., 'will never be able to...', 'I miss him/her here') that strongly implies death, use this guidance.
content: When a statement euphemistically implies a person has died without explicitly saying so, also extract the implied state that the person is likely deceased, in addition to the literal statement.
Record the inference with an appropriate hedge (e.g., 'likely deceased') because the speaker did not state it directly; do not assert cause, date, or circumstances of death.
Stop after capturing the likely-deceased state and the literal content; do not extrapolate further details about the person or the relationship.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Origin Events as Distinct Memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user explains how they started or got into an activity, hobby, or interest, including who introduced it or when it began.
content: During extraction, if a message contains an origin narrative (how the person started an activity, who introduced it, what prompted it, or a concrete start time), create a separate event memory for the origin in addition to any preference or state memory.
Record the causal source (person or circumstance) and the start time/age if stated; do not fold the origin into a generic preference summary.
If the origin names another person, also consider a relationship memory capturing that connection.
Emit at most one origin memory per activity per message; skip if the same origin is repeated later.
